target_state: FUN_00f999e0 @ 0x00f999e0 is the method at slot +0x50 of the class table whose address is 0x01490be8 (read out of the image; the single xref comes from 0x01490c38 = 0x01490be8 + 0x50, this body's own slot). It is a zero-argument __thiscall predicate with no direct callers recorded: it is reached only through the table. The body is 80 instructions, 0x00f999e0..0x00f99ab3 inclusive (212 bytes), and it is five gates followed by a 24-group float scan: (1) a global getter at 0x00f48a70 whose return value becomes the RECEIVER of a zero-argument thiscall at 0x00f699b0, whose AL must be nonzero; (2) the table word at slot +0x4c, called with the byte 7, whose AL must be zero; (3) the receiver's byte at +0x370, which must be zero; (4) the table word at slot +0x30, whose AL must be nonzero; (5) the receiver's byte at +0x4f4, which must be nonzero. Then 24 four-float groups are compared as two pairs each and the body returns 0 at the first group whose BOTH pairs are ordered-equal, and 1 only if every gate held and no group did. Nothing in the body writes memory: the only memory write in all 80 instructions is the PUSH 0x7 onto the stack. Reconstruction is complete and self-verified; the open items are evidence ceilings, not gaps in the body.

intended_paths.status: staging-only handoff; no canonical path is claimed and no other package's files were touched

implementation.argument_surface: the receiver in ECX, and NOTHING else. Zero ordinary stack arguments. The three return sites (0x00f999f6, 0x00f99aae, 0x00f99ab3) are all a bare `C3` with no immediate, and the one word the body pushes -- `PUSH 0x7` at 0x00f999fc -- is never dropped by the body, so at both of the later return sites the ESP in effect is entry-4 and the bare RET consumes exactly the return address. Ghidra's own record reports "undefined FUN_00f999e0(void)" with ghidra_parameter_count 0, which is its reading of an unclassified convention and not a claim that the body takes no argument; abi_derived.conventions gives confidence INFERRED with corroboration not_available and candidates __thiscall/__fastcall.
implementation.receiver_model: an OPAQUE byte run and nothing else, because the machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only (register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, offsets [0, 880, 1076, 1080, 1084, 1088, 1172, 1176, 1180, 1184, 1268], max_offset 1268, written_through 0). No struct member is named anywhere in this package; every receiver access goes through word_value_at / byte_at / real_at with the displacement as a named constexpr. The record's eleven displacements are the two flag bytes, the table word and the four floats of outer index 0's two DIRECT groups; the four floats it does not list are the two INNER groups, and the reason is visible in the listing rather than guessed -- see mechanics.group_layout_why_the_record_is_blind. The receiver is READ-ONLY for this body and the model test asserts that byte for byte.
implementation.dispatch_model: two sites, both the canonical two-level x86-32 shape and both classified VTABLE_SLOT by the tooling: `MOV EAX,[ESI]` / `MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x4c]` / `CALL EDX` at 0x00f999f7..0x00f99a00, and the same again with 0x30 at 0x00f99a0e..0x00f99a15. The word at the receiver's +0x00 is a table ADDRESS; the slot displacement indexes that table. The table this class uses is 0x01490be8 and the entries it holds at +0x4c and +0x30 are 0x00fa0e60 and 0x00fa0d80, both read out of the image. Those two addresses are deliberately NOT called by name in the reconstruction: the transfer is through whatever word the RUNTIME object holds, and a derived class may override either slot. What the reconstruction does is call through the receiver's own +0x00, read TWICE with the first table call in between, which is what the listing does. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 2, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0.
implementation.dependency_note: both direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the model test, so the reconstruction links without them only in the model test's translation unit. 0x00f48a70 is a six-byte cdecl leaf; 0x00f699b0 is a zero-argument thiscall on ECX. Neither is open, and no callee of either was needed to settle anything this body claims.

observed_original_abi.return_register: AL (one byte), a machine fact and not a modelling choice: all three exits write AL only. The machine record's own claim is XMM0; it is kept in return_semantics and its refutation in return_note.

observed_original_abi.exception_frame: none. No FS:[0] install, no trylevel word, and the body is 212 bytes of straight arithmetic and calls. abi_derived.seh_or_cookie_frame is false.
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: ghidra_has_calling_convention is false, ghidra_calling_convention_signal is no_information, ghidra_parameter_count is 0 and return_type_resolved is false, so Ghidra contributes nothing here. observed_original_abi.dispatch: two indirect transfers, both CALL EDX, both two-level table loads: 0x00f99a00 through slot 0x4c and 0x00f99a15 through slot 0x30. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 2, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, which agrees with the listing's own count of two.
observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: 0x00f48a70: cdecl, six bytes, `A1 B0 8E 6C 01 / C3` = MOV EAX,ds:0x16c8eb0 ; RET. No stack argument, no ECX use, EAX its only register written. 0x00f699b0: __thiscall on ECX with no stack argument; its body reads [ECX+0x1ce] and [ECX+ESI*1+0x78] and never a stack displacement, and both of its terminators are POP ESI ; RET. The two table slots: 0x00fa0e60 at +0x4c ends `C2 04 00` (RET 0x4) and reads its argument as a byte with `MOV DL,[ESP+0x4]` at 0x00fa0e66, so the +0x4c callee owns the one word this body pushes; 0x00fa0d80 at +0x30 ends a bare `C3` and takes none.
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: INFERRED for the convention and the receiver (abi_derived.conventions.confidence INFERRED, corroboration not_available; receiver.confidence INFERRED); OBSERVED for the listing, the parse and the disassembly, which are the two-level load, the operand displacements, the two CALLs, the three terminators and the absence of every memory-destination operand.
observed_original_abi.return_type_is_the_machine_claim_not_a_c: SUPERSEDED BY THE rp10 REPAIR, and kept as a record of what changed rather than deleted. This field used to read: "This field transcribes what the MACHINE record claims and is deliberately not a C type. abi.return_register is XMM0 and abi.return_semantics is float_or_x87_in_XMM0, both at APPROXIMATION, and inference RT1 gives the reason verbatim: 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body'. I did NOT replace it with a type, because writing a clean type into abi.return_type would move the check by fiat." That reasoning was half right: moving the check by fiat would be wrong, but the field was being filled with a REGISTER-CLASS PHRASE where the tooling defines a TYPE, and no C++ declaration can ever equal a register class. abi.return_type is now "std::uint8_t" -- the type the source span declares AND the type the listing proves, so nothing was moved by fiat -- and the phrase itself is preserved verbatim in abi.return_semantics, with abi.return_register still naming XMM0. The claim is relocated, not deleted and not adopted. A typedef named after the phrase was never written and must never be: it would restore the string agreement with nothing behind it. What the listing fixes is below.
observed_original_abi.return_width_from_the_listing: one byte: the returned value is 0x00 or 0x01 in AL. All three exits write AL only -- XOR AL,AL at 0x00f999f3, MOV AL,0x1 at 0x00f99aab and XOR AL,AL at 0x00f99ab0 -- and no instruction on any path writes the other three bytes of the return register; inside the scan, MOVSS and UCOMISS touch XMM0 and EFLAGS only. The reconstruction therefore declares std::uint8_t, which asserts the width and nothing about the register, and records the disagreement with the record's phrase in return_semantics.record_disagreement and in unresolved_questions item 1.

mechanics.body_shape: five straight-line gates, then a 6-iteration outer loop each holding a 2-iteration inner loop and two unrolled groups, with three return sites: 0x00f999f3 (reached from 0x00f999f1, 0x00f99a04, 0x00f99a0c, 0x00f99a19 and 0x00f99a22 -- five incoming edges), 0x00f99aaf (reached from the three JP instructions at 0x00f99a5b, 0x00f99a81 and 0x00f99a9f) and 0x00f99aab (the fall-through of the outer loop).

gates.1: 00f999e3 CALL 0x00f48a70 -> EAX; 00f999e8 MOV ECX,EAX; 00f999ea CALL 0x00f699b0. Zero-argument thiscall on the value the getter returned -- a DIFFERENT object, one level below this function's own receiver, and not a member of it. 00f999ef TEST AL,AL / 00f999f1 JNZ 0x00f999f7: all EIGHT bits of AL, and a clear AL returns 0.
gates.2: 00f999f7/00f999f9/00f999fc/00f999fe/00f99a00: the receiver's word at +0x00, the table word at its +0x4c, `PUSH 0x7`, ECX = the receiver, CALL EDX. 00f99a02 TEST AL,AL / 00f99a04 JNZ 0x00f999f3: the OPPOSITE polarity to gate 1 -- a NONZERO AL returns 0.
gates.3: 00f99a06 CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0x370],AL / 00f99a0c JNZ 0x00f999f3. The comparison is against AL and not against an immediate, and AL is provably zero there: 00f99a02's TEST together with 00f99a04's JNZ not taken means the byte the slot returned is 0x00. A nonzero byte at the receiver's +0x370 returns 0.
gates.4: 00f99a0e/00f99a10/00f99a13/00f99a15: the table word read AGAIN, and its +0x30, with NO argument word pushed. 00f99a17 TEST AL,AL / 00f99a19 JZ 0x00f999f3: a zero AL returns 0.
gates.5: 00f99a1b CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0x4f4],0x0 / 00f99a22 JZ 0x00f999f3, against an immediate this time. A zero byte at the receiver's +0x4f4 returns 0.

mechanics.table: The receiver's word at +0x00 is read at 0x00f999f7 and again at 0x00f99a0e, with the +0x4c call in between, and the reconstruction re-reads it for exactly that reason. The table this class uses is at 0x01490be8; read out of the image with `objdump -s -j .rdata --start-address=0x01490be8 --stop-address=0x01490c50`, its entries are 0x00fa0d50, 0x00fa0f10, 0x00641770, 0x00967e70, 0x00fa0d60, 0x0104c110, 0x00fa0d70, 0x00fa0d90, 0x00fa0da0, 0x00f99ee0, 0x00931ac0, 0x00fa0d40, 0x00fa0d80, 0x00f96870, 0x00f96cd0, 0x00f96d10, 0x00f99980, 0x00fa0e10, 0x00fa0e40, 0x00fa0e60, 0x00f999e0, 0x00fa6c60, 0x00fa5040, 0x00f975d0, 0x00fa6ec0, 0x00fa7220 for slots +0x00 .. +0x64. So +0x30 holds 0x00fa0d80, +0x4c holds 0x00fa0e60, and +0x50 holds 0x00f999e0 -- this body, which is where the record's single xref from 0x01490c38 comes from. That address is a vtable association from the record, corroborated here by the image; the reconstruction models the SLOT, not the entry.
mechanics.group_layout: Four four-float groups per outer iteration, at outer_cursor - 0xc4, outer_cursor - 0x64, outer_cursor - 0x4 and outer_cursor + 0x5c, where outer_cursor = receiver + 0x438 + 0x10*i. Consecutive bases are 0x60 apart, which is also the inner stride at 00f99a5e. A group base g is read as four floats at g, g+4, g+8 and g+0xc, compared as the pairs (g, g+8) and (g+4, g+0xc). With outer_stride 0x10 and 6 outer indices, the 24 bases are receiver + 0x374 + 0x10k for k = 0..23 -- the four families above are this run at k = 0, 6, 12 and 18, because the inner stride 0x60 is exactly six times the outer stride 0x10. The scan therefore spans receiver + 0x374 .. receiver + 0x4f0, and 0x4f0 + 4 = 0x4f4 is the fifth gate's byte.
mechanics.group_layout_corroboration: 0x00f699b0, this body's OWN second direct callee, repeats the identical shape in the same image: `LEA EDX,[ECX+0x84]` then the same LAHF / TEST AH,0x44 / JNP-then-JP idiom over (base, base+8) and (base+4, base+0xc) at a 0x60 group stride (00f699d8, 00f699e7, 00f699f5, 00f69a04), with `INC ESI / ADD EDX,0x10 / CMP ESI,0x6 / JL` (00f69a13..00f69a1a) and `MOV AL,0x1` at 00f69a1c. Its first group base is ECX+0x80 and its second is ECX+0xe0, i.e. the same 0x60 delta this body uses, and its per-iteration flag gate is `CMP BYTE PTR [ECX+ESI*1+0x78],0`, the same shape as this body's +0x370 gate. That is an independent listing, not this body's own evidence, and it is used here only to confirm the group shape and the compare polarity.
mechanics.group_layout_why_the_record_is_blind: The machine-derived receiver record enumerates eleven displacements: 0x0, 0x370, 0x434, 0x438, 0x43c, 0x440, 0x494, 0x498, 0x49c, 0x4a0 and 0x4f4. Those are the table word, the two flag bytes, the outer cursor 0x438, and the four floats of each of outer index 0's two DIRECT groups. The two INNER groups' floats are absent, and the reason is in the listing rather than in a guess: the alias-aware scan that produced the record loses the ESI alias at `POP ESI` on the first return path (00f999f5), because a POP is a write to ESI, and 00f999f7's `MOV EAX,[ESI]` is after it. So the record is blind to every access from 0x00f999f7 onward -- it is not contradicting the layout derived here, and `evidence_fields`' alias-aware scan over the same listing independently reports zero receiver displacements for the same reason. The listing is the authority and the derived layout is asserted from it, instruction by instruction, in the .cpp.
mechanics.compare_loop: Every compare is the same eleven instructions: UCOMISS XMM0,[m32]; LAHF; TEST AH,0x44; JNP-or-JP. UCOMISS leaves (ZF,PF) at (0,0) for less and for greater, (1,0) for equal and (1,1) for unordered, so AH & 0x44 is 0x00, 0x40 or 0x44 and TEST overwrites the parity with the parity of THAT value -- 0x00 has zero bits set and 0x44 has two, both even (PF=0), while 0x40 has one (PF=1). Therefore JNP is taken exactly when the pair is NOT ordered-equal, and missed exactly when it IS. In the pair-0 blocks the branch is JNP and the fall-through is the pair-1 block, so pair 1 is examined only when pair 0 IS ordered-equal; in the pair-1 blocks the branch is JP, which is taken exactly when that pair IS ordered-equal, and it targets 0x00f99aaf, which returns 0. So a group rejects iff BOTH of its pairs are ordered-equal. C++ `==` on float is false for unordered and is therefore the machine's test exactly, and the reconstruction uses it directly. The two cases where a byte-wise reading of the same four bytes disagrees are +0.0f against -0.0f (ordered-equal, so the group rejects; the bytes differ) and a quiet NaN against its own bit pattern (unordered, so the group passes; the bytes are identical). The body never writes MXCSR, so the default applies and a denormal compares normally; that is stated and not modelled.
mechanics.compare_loop_decompiler_disagreement: Ghidra's decompilation renders the same eleven instructions as `if (pfVar6[-1] != pfVar6[1]) { fVar2 = *pfVar6; if (fVar2 != *pfVar1) return uVar3; }`, i.e. the fall-through on the NOT-equal side and the early return on the both-UNEQUAL side -- the exact complement. The complement is not a harmless alternative reading: it rejects a group where only one pair is equal, and accepts a group where neither is. The listing is followed here, the flag arithmetic above is the argument, and mechanics.group_layout_corroboration is a second listing that agrees with the listing rather than with the decompilation.
mechanics.control_flow: Twelve conditional branches (JNZ x3, JZ x3, JNP x3, JP x3) plus one unconditional JMP, and every target lies inside 0x00f999e0..0x00f99ab3. 00f99a2d's `LEA ECX,[ECX]` (bytes 8D 09) is a two-byte no-op and 00f99a38's `JMP 00f99a40` is the loop rotation; neither is modelled as work. The outer loop's back edge (00f99aa8) targets 00f99a30, which is the inner counter's zeroing and not 00f99a2d, so the no-op is skipped on every iteration after the first.
mechanics.loop_bounds: `CMP EDX,0x2` at 00f99a61 and `CMP EDI,0x6` at 00f99aa5, both a SIGNED JL against a counter incremented first, so the inner loop visits exactly indices 0 and 1 and the outer exactly 0..5. Nothing else in the body can change either count.
mechanics.receiver_writes: none. All 80 instructions were read for a memory-destination operand: every `MOVSS`/`UCOMISS` is a read, both `MOV EAX,[ESI]` are reads, both `MOV EDX,[EAX+...]` are reads, and both `CMP BYTE PTR [ESI+...]` are reads. The one memory write in the body is `PUSH 0x7` onto the stack. abi_derived.receiver.written_through is 0, and the model test compares the whole modelled receiver before and after on three different exit paths.
mechanics.return_word: All three exits write AL only -- `XOR AL,AL` at 00f999f3, `MOV AL,0x1` at 00f99aab and `XOR AL,AL` at 00f99ab0 -- and no instruction in the scan writes the return register at all, since MOVSS and UCOMISS touch XMM0 and EFLAGS only. So bits 8..31 of the return register are, on every path, the last callee's word with its low byte cleared, and the declared 1-byte type promises only the low byte. The model publishes the whole word through dead_return_word() and the model test poisons each callee in turn to separate the two halves.
mechanics.globals: none in this body's span. The one global it touches is read inside 0x00f48a70 (`MOV EAX,ds:0x16c8eb0`), which is a different VA and a different body's span; no instruction in these 80 names a data-segment address, and validate._data_addresses over the span finds none. GLOBALS is therefore declared empty, which is a statement about THIS body and not a claim that 0x16c8eb0 is unused.
mechanics.vtable_note: The record carries vtables.referenced_by_vtables = ["vtable:0x01490be8"] and the single xref at 0x01490c38. Both were confirmed against the image (mechanics.table) and the association is used to name the SLOT displacements' table, not to type anything: the two entries are deliberately not called by name in the reconstruction because the runtime object may hold overrides. The check itself is corroborated from the listing and from abi_derived.dispatch, both of which the reconstruction agrees with.

global_read_by_direct_callee_1.role: the single global 0x00f48a70 reads, in `MOV EAX,ds:0x16c8eb0`; its value becomes the RECEIVER of 0x00f699b0 at 00f999e8. Read from the image, not from any record. The value it holds at run time is not established by anything in this package and is not claimed.

vtable_read_by_this_body.role: the class table this body is a member of. It is the value the receiver's word at +0x00 holds at run time, and this body occupies its slot +0x50 (0x00f999e0), which is where the record's single xref from 0x01490c38 comes from. Its entries at +0x30 and +0x4c are 0x00fa0d80 and 0x00fa0e60. Confirmed by reading the .rdata bytes; recorded for the integrator and NOT modelled, because the reconstruction calls through whatever word the receiver's own +0x00 names.

return_semantics.value: 1 if and only if all five gates held and none of the twenty-four four-float groups had both of its pairs ordered-equal; 0 otherwise. The three exits are 0x00f999f3 (XOR AL,AL), 0x00f99aaf (XOR AL,AL) and 0x00f99aab (MOV AL,0x1).
return_semantics.record_disagreement: STILL UNRESOLVED, relocated rather than settled (rp10). The machine record's own claim is abi.return_register "XMM0" with return_semantics "float_or_x87_in_XMM0", both at APPROXIMATION, and inference RT1 gives the same reason verbatim: "an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body". The listing refutes it -- XMM0 is written only by the six MOVSS and read only by the six UCOMISS, no path leaves a value in it, and every exit writes AL alone -- but a refutation is still not an agreement, and that is why the phrase is retained rather than corrected: it is the machine layer's claim, verbatim, and overriding it is not this package's to do. What changed in this repair is only WHICH FIELD holds it. abi.return_type is the projection's TYPE field, read by the RETURN SEMANTICS check and compared against one C++ return type captured from the source span, so a register-class phrase there guaranteed a WARN no matter how correct the reconstruction was; the phrase is a classification and now lives in abi.return_semantics, where the projection's own documentation puts register classes, and abi.return_type states std::uint8_t, which the listing proves rather than merely permits. The reconstruction declares std::uint8_t and always did: nothing about the body, the branches, the constants, the displacements, the callees or the argument order moved. No typedef named after the phrase was written, because that would win the string comparison with no evidence behind it. The disagreement with the machine layer survives in full and is tracked as unresolved_questions item 1.
return_semantics.ownership: the body acquires and releases nothing. It reads a pointer out of a global via a callee and passes addresses to three callees; whether any of those objects is owned, borrowed or a smart handle is not established by any record for this target and is not claimed.
return_semantics.lifetime: the only frame objects are the pushed selector word (a dword at entry+4, owned by the +0x4c callee, whose `RET 0x4` consumes it) and the saved ESI and EDI, both popped on every path that pushed them. Nothing is allocated and nothing escapes.

types: Receiver -- an opaque byte run, one unnamed array, no member named anywhere in this package (the machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only)
SlotFirst -- Word (__thiscall *)(Receiver*, std::uint8_t), the shape of the table word at slot +0x4c, the one word it takes being callee-popped
SlotSecond -- Word (__thiscall *)(Receiver*), the shape of the table word at slot +0x30, taking no word
Word -- std::uint32_t, a 32-bit table entry and a 32-bit receiver word
Real -- float, binary32, because MOVSS and UCOMISS each read four bytes

evidence.classification: primary-binary static analysis; no runtime validation
evidence.assembly: the 80 instructions of mechanics.function_extent, re-derived from the image with objdump -d -M intel --start-address=0x00f999e0 --stop-address=0x00f99ab4 and identical to the committed listing at every address, mnemonic, operand, call target and branch target
evidence.decompiler: the committed decompilation of this VA, used as a hint and OVERRULED on the compare polarity -- see mechanics.compare_loop_decompiler_disagreement. Ghidra's prototype for the VA is "undefined FUN_00f999e0(void)" with ghidra_parameter_count 0, which is its reading of an unclassified convention and not a claim about the argument surface or the return value.
evidence.decompiler_disagreements: one, and it is load-bearing: Ghidra inverts both polarities of the eleven-instruction compare idiom, rendering `if (left != right) { if (left2 != right2) return 0; }` where the listing gives `if (left == right) { if (left2 == right2) return 0; }`. A second, cosmetic: Ghidra renders the LAHF/TEST parity dance as a 24-bit CONCAT shift into uVar3, which is its own encoding of the same flags and is not a value the body computes.

known_blockers: THE ASSIGNED BLOCKER IS GONE (rp21): the promotion gate's clang++ build failed with `error: unused variable 'kInnerCount' [-Werror,-Wunused-const-variable]` at sw2_00f999e0_model_test.cpp:445. The constant is the harness's copy of the inner loop's trip count, documented in place as `CMP EDX,0x2`, and it had become unused because group_bases() hard-codes the four group families by hand. THE FACT WAS NOT DELETED -- it is a real claim and it is now PINNED IN TWO PLACES, which is what the contract's option (a) asks for. (1) Three static_asserts next to the constant bind it to the instruction form that fixes it: `kInnerCount == 2` with the message naming `CMP EDX,0x2` at 0x00f99a61 (a signed JL against a counter zeroed at 0x00f99a30 and incremented at 0x00f99a5d BEFORE the compare), plus `kGroup0Base + (kInnerCount - 1) * kGroupStride == kGroup1Base` and `kGroup1Base + kGroupStride == kGroup2Base`, so a kInnerCount that disagreed with the group families is now a BUILD error instead of a silently differently-shaped fixture. (2) A new sub-case of K, 'the inner trip count, from the inside', drives the constant at RUNTIME: for every one of the six outer indices it derives each of the kInnerCount inner rows as bases[0] + row*kGroupStride, requires that to be the harness's own family bases[row], requires every row to sit below the first unrolled group, and requires the address one row FURTHER to be exactly the first unrolled group's base. It then names the discriminating address: at the TOP outer index the last inner row is receiver + 0x424, whose nearest outer row-0 base is outer index 11 -- an index the six-iteration outer loop never takes -- so only the inner loop's second row can produce it, and a rejecting group planted there must return 0. That is the runtime half of what `CMP EDX,0x2` fixes, and it is the assertion that rules out a single-step inner loop without relying on the count being read positionally. The aliasing that stops the address set from pinning the count from ABOVE is asserted there too, so the limit of the evidence is on the record rather than only in a comment. SECOND, PRE-EXISTING BLOCKER FOUND AND NOT FIXED (rp21): with the build error gone, the §5 reproduction runs the test to completion under clang++ and reports exactly ONE failing check, `C: the body pushes an argument word for +0x4c and none for +0x30`, which asserts `g_stub_esp_30 > g_stub_esp_4c`. That assertion is a claim about the COMPILER's stack layout, not about the machine. MEASURED, g++: esp_30 - esp_4c = +16. MEASURED, clang++: esp_30 - esp_4c = 0. Clang places the __thiscall argument in an outgoing-args FRAME SLOT (`movl $7,(%esp)`) instead of pushing it, and emits `sub $0x4,%esp` after the call to account for the callee's pop, so both table call sites sit at the SAME stack level; g++ emits `subl $12,%esp ; pushl $7 ; call *%edx ; addl $12,%esp` and the two levels differ. The machine's own relation IS a strict ordering (PUSH 0x7 puts the +0x4c callee four bytes lower and the callee's RET 0x4 gives the level back), and the substantive evidence for it survives on both compilers: `g_stub_arg_word_4c == kSelector` is measured out of the callee's own entry+4 and passes. But the SIGN of the ESP difference is unrecoverable under clang's calling sequence, so no compiler-independent reformulation of that assertion exists -- the alternatives (a `>=`, or `g_stub_arg_word_30 != kSelector`) are strictly weaker, and the contract forbids weakening an assertion, so this is reported rather than patched. It reproduces on a faithful pre-edit copy of the package, so it is not a consequence of the kInnerCount repair. RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION for the parent: this check is a harness-construction defect, not a reconstruction defect -- re-express case C's second claim as something the machine fixes and both compilers exhibit (the +0x30 callee's entry+4 is not a body-written selector word), or drop the ESP comparison and keep the entry+4 measurement, with the substitution recorded here.

A THIRD, PRE-EXISTING DEFECT WAS ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME FILE, BECAUSE IT MASKED THE ONE ABOVE (rp21): under clang++ the test SEGFAULTED instead of reporting anything, so no other result was observable. THE FIX IS ONE LINE IN THE FIXTURE: build_hostile_table now plants the zero-stack-word decoy decoy_elsewhere_second at +0x30 and the one-word decoy at every other index. The table still holds a decoy at EVERY index and the +0x30 slot still holds a decoy -- which is the whole point of case D -- and no assertion was touched, added or removed; only the decoy's arity now matches the slot it occupies, so a wrong dispatch is caught and reported instead of being fatal. The complete fix is for each decoy to be an asm thunk that reads its own return address and pops four only when it was reached from the +0x4c site, which makes the decoys arity-agnostic; that is a harness redesign rather than a source-shape repair and was left to the parent.
